summary: The WhatsApp allowlist owner sends the direct-rule change as an RFC 7396 merge patch (explicit null for a removed rule or field), so lowering a scope or removing a contact really removes its prompt on the S24 Gateway.
reason: S24 26/10 14:25:59Z, operation sadok-scope-standard-20261026 (Amine: remove Sadok's Zain Bahrain custom scope): the owner sent the whole channels.whatsapp.direct map under replacePaths, but the Gateway's config.patch (OpenClaw 2026.9.6 applyMergePatch) merges objects and replacePaths only replaces arrays. The Gateway logged « config.patch noop (no changed paths) », verification failed, the receipt was indeterminate and the contact kept its custom prompt and metadata (effect verified absent). Any scope lowering, suspension or removal that drops a direct rule had the same defect; the test Gateway replaced the map wholesale and hid it.

tests.name: installer/termux-lite/test-whatsapp-allowlist.py
tests.evidence: 48 tests. The fake Gateway now applies the real merge semantics (objects merge, null removes). New test: custom -> standard keeps the rule's other field, removes only systemPrompt, sends {number:{systemPrompt:null}} without replacePaths on the map, receipt updated. Without the fix 4 tests fail (scope lowering and both delete paths), as on the S24.
